item.company: University of Virginia – UVA Northern Virginia
item.title: Education and Outreach Professional
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 9/29/2026.

Note: No visa sponsorship. Fully on-site in Fairfax, VA. Cover letter and resume required. Apply online searching for requisition number R0086806.

UVA Northern Virginia is based in the Washington Capital region and supports all University of Virginia schools in their educational and non-educational programmatic efforts, including degree and non-degree programs, research, public talks, and community events. The Education and Outreach Professional manages operational and strategic engagement with clients offering educational programs, with end-to-end project ownership from conception through delivery and post-program accounting. 1-3 years of relevant experience required. Salary $55,000-$65,000.

Key responsibilities include: scheduling and leading meetings with internal and external partners interested in utilizing UVA Northern Virginia facilities; working with clients to develop proposals and contracts for services to be delivered; communicating verbally and in writing with internal and external clients; servicing clients' pre-program and in-service needs including space requests, catering needs, and custom requests; working with facilities personnel to ensure seamless delivery; partnering with internal teammates in a collaborative and entrepreneurial unit; delivering customer service skills including problem-solving to meet customer requests; and accountability for all aspects of program delivery.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree required (degree in a field related to education, marketing, or service operations preferred); 1-3 years of relevant customer-facing or higher education experience; direct, customer-facing work in a service operation preferred. No visa sponsorship.

Compensation and logistics: salary $55,000-$65,000 commensurate with education and experience. Comprehensive UVA benefits. Fully on-site in Fairfax, VA. Cover letter and resume required (upload together). Apply via UVA jobs portal, requisition R0086806.

item.title: Senior Director, UVA Northern Virginia
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 9/29/2026.

IMPORTANT: This is a senior role requiring 7+ years of related professional experience including 3+ years of formal managerial experience. It is not suitable for early- or mid-career candidates. Note: this is a restricted position contingent upon funding availability. Fully on-site in Fairfax, VA. Cover letter and resume required. Apply online searching for requisition number R0087089.

The University of Virginia seeks a Senior Director for the UVA Northern Virginia initiative. Reporting to the Dean, the Senior Director will assist in leading the strategic direction of education for UVA Northern Virginia, developing and promoting a broad array of educational initiatives including synchronous and asynchronous online and in-person offerings, and overseeing the planning, scheduling, and coordination of these programs. The position manages a team of 4 FTE. Salary $130,000-$155,000.

Key responsibilities include: establishing and monitoring performance metrics and operational dashboards to evaluate program effectiveness, campus utilization, enrollment, and strategic initiatives; providing leadership and coordination for the development, implementation, and ongoing support of new and existing educational programs, collaborating with academic leaders and centralized university partners across admissions, enrollment, marketing, instructional technology, information systems, library, and student support services; developing, managing, and monitoring operating budgets, financial forecasts, and resource allocation; directing campus operations including facilities management, space planning, capital improvement coordination, safety and security, business continuity, operational policies, and the management of contracts and external service providers; developing strategic partnerships with academic units, government agencies, healthcare systems, corporations, economic development organizations, and community stakeholders; and managing and developing a team of 4 FTE.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree required (master's degree preferred); 7+ years of related professional experience including 3+ years of formal managerial experience; demonstrated experience managing complex operating budgets, financial planning, forecasting, and resource allocation; demonstrated success leading cross-functional teams and managing complex organizational operations within higher education or similarly complex organizations; and experience building strategic partnerships with external organizations, government agencies, and industry leaders.

Compensation and logistics: salary $130,000-$155,000 commensurate with education and experience. Comprehensive UVA benefits. Fully on-site in Fairfax, VA. Restricted position (contingent on funding). Cover letter and resume required. Apply via UVA jobs portal, requisition R0087089.

item.title: Kindergarten ESL Teacher (China)
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 9/29/2026.

Note: This is a teaching abroad position based in China. Primary intake is February 2027. Applicants must be native English speakers from the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, or South Africa. A TEFL/TESOL/CELTA certificate is required. Applications from both individuals and couples are welcome. Apply by sending a CV and introduction video to kira@talent-e.com.cn.

Talent-E Education is an education company located in Shenzhen, China dedicated to helping foreign teachers integrate smoothly into life in China. Partner kindergartens are located across China including Shenzhen, Guangzhou, Shanghai, Beijing, and other Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. As a Kindergarten ESL Teacher, you will work with children aged 2 to 6, helping them build confidence and communication skills through fun, interactive lessons, supported by one to three local teaching assistants in each class.

Key responsibilities include: creating engaging, age-appropriate English lessons; fostering a fun, safe, and positive learning environment; managing classroom routines and encouraging student participation; tracking student progress and providing feedback; and contributing to classroom decoration and teaching materials. Working schedule: Monday-Friday, 8:00 AM-5:30 PM (with 1-2 hour lunch break); 40 working hours/week; weekends off.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree (Education, Linguistics, or Psychology preferred); native English speaker from the US, Canada, UK, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, or South Africa; TEFL/TESOL/CELTA certificate required; teaching experience with young children ages 2-6 preferred; clean criminal background check; and strong communication and classroom management skills.

Compensation and logistics: salary 12,000-20,000 CNY/month (~$1,650-$2,750 USD/month). Benefits include paid summer/winter vacations and public holidays, academic training and orientation, health insurance, flight allowance, free hotel accommodation upon arrival, apartment hunting support, and a foreign teacher community. China (Shenzhen, Guangzhou, Shanghai, Beijing, and other cities). February 2027 intake. Apply: CV and introduction video to kira@talent-e.com.cn.

item.title: Youth Development Specialist – El Salvador
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 9/29/2026.

Note: Peace Corps Volunteers receive a living stipend, not a salary. This is a two-year volunteer commitment requiring U.S. citizenship. Volunteers live and work in host communities, receiving a stipend and other support including housing, medical care, and a readjustment allowance upon completion of service.

The Peace Corps is seeking U.S. citizens to serve as Youth Development Specialists in El Salvador. Youth make up more than a quarter of El Salvador's population, yet many young people face social and economic challenges including economic hardship, low school completion rates, limited life skills development opportunities, and barriers to civic engagement. Only half of youth complete lower secondary school and even fewer complete upper secondary school. As a Youth Development Specialist, you will collaborate with school staff to equip youth with essential life skills such as communication, empathy, creative problem-solving, and goal setting, working alongside community leaders to create supportive environments that encourage youth participation in community projects and civic engagement.

Key responsibilities include: collaborating with school staff to teach essential life skills to youth; working alongside community leaders to create supportive environments for youth participation; contributing to community projects and civic engagement initiatives; building relationships with host community members; and exchanging knowledge and helping transform lives for future generations.

Qualifications: U.S. citizenship required; bachelor's degree (typical requirement for Peace Corps service); demonstrated commitment to community development, education, or youth work. Visit the Peace Corps El Salvador project page for full details and application information.

Compensation and logistics: living stipend provided (not a salary); additional benefits include housing support, medical and dental care, language and cultural training, and a readjustment allowance upon completion of service. El Salvador. 2-year commitment. U.S. citizenship required.

item.description:

Note: Salary not stated (federal Non-Appropriated Fund/NAF pay scale; confirm via the application portal). Official college transcripts (showing degree awarded/conferred) must be submitted at time of application -- diplomas and degree audits are not acceptable. This is a Non-Appropriated Fund (NAF) position; NAF employment does not lead to federal civil service status. Position may be available at multiple Navy installation locations.

The Navy Child and Youth Programs (CYP) Training and Curriculum (T&C) Specialist provides comprehensive staff training, assists in monitoring developmentally appropriate curriculum for children and youth ages 6 weeks to 18 years, and promotes career and education opportunities for professional growth. A bachelor's degree in child development or early childhood education plus 3 years of experience working with children and/or youth is required.

Key responsibilities include (Training): serving as a lead participant in achieving and maintaining DoD certification and national accreditation; developing, coordinating, and delivering a comprehensive training program to expand the knowledge, skills, abilities, and competencies of individuals assigned to work with children and youth; arranging for subject matter experts to conduct specialized training; identifying ongoing training needs and tailoring training plans accordingly; maintaining training records and individual development plans; and developing programs that encourage pursuit of continuing higher education including Child Development Associate (CDA) and Military School-Age Credential (MSA). (Classroom/Programming Support): monitoring and providing quality assurance for the development and implementation of curriculum, activity plans, schedules, and routines; observing, reviewing, evaluating, and modifying activities and plans for appropriateness; providing direction and support for CYP professionals; advising appropriate behavior management techniques; facilitating inclusion of children who require accommodations; and monitoring the implementation of Inclusion Support Plans (ISPs).

Qualifications: a bachelor's or higher degree in child development or early childhood education plus 3 years of full-time experience working with children and/or youth (or a combination of education and experience including at least 24 higher-level semester hours in a child-related field plus 3 years of experience); knowledge of early childhood or youth education principles; knowledge of adult learning techniques; knowledge of Federal and State laws governing child abuse and neglect detection and prevention; and ability to communicate effectively in English. Official transcripts required at application.

Compensation and logistics: salary not stated (federal NAF pay scale). NAF benefits package. Multiple Navy installation locations. Official transcripts required at time of application.

item.title: Lead Writer, Executive Office
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 10/16/2026.

IMPORTANT: This is a senior role requiring a minimum of five years of relevant work experience, including experience providing staff support for executive leaders. It is not suitable for early-career candidates.

The Brookings Institution is one of the most influential and trusted think tanks in the world. The Executive Office (EO) moves the Brookings mission forward by supporting and guiding the research programs, external affairs, and business operations of the Institution. The Lead Writer serves as the primary writer for the Brookings president and the executive office, working closely with the Vice President of Communications and Public Affairs. This is a key role combining expert-level writing with strong project management skills. The position is primarily in-person at the Washington, DC office (generally 4-5 days/week; occasional remote may be permitted). Salary $84,200-$93,000. Cover letter and resume required as one document.

Key responsibilities include (70% President's Communications and Presentation Development): serving as the president's speechwriter and managing development of the president's presentations to key audiences; preparing the president for events as a speaker, panel moderator, or fireside chat participant through gathering and synthesizing information, fact-checking, and tailoring language to reflect the president's voice; writing concise (3-5 minute) opening or closing remarks for internal or external events; collaborating with the president on additional speeches and talking points including graduation/commencement speeches and donor meeting preparation; ensuring consistent presidential messaging across communications products; owning the process of preparing presentations for stakeholder audiences including board of trustees meetings and all-staff town halls; developing scripts and talking points for all-staff town halls; and working closely with communications colleagues to draft social media posts from the president's accounts. (30% Written Communications and Correspondence): writing, editing, and sending all-staff email communications from the president; working closely with the development team to draft and send emails from the president's account to funders and potential funders; writing and sending invitations to high-level external speakers invited to speak at Brookings; and providing support to the Vice President of Communications and Public Affairs on written communications as workload allows.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree in Communications, Journalism, English, Political Science, or a related public-policy field required (master's degree desirable); minimum five years of relevant work experience required including experience providing staff support for executive leaders; exceptional writing, storytelling, and editing skills with the ability to adapt voice and tone to match the speaker; strategic thinker with the ability to distill complex ideas into clear, impactful messages; proven ability to advise senior leaders with confidence and discretion; experience working in fast-paced, high-stakes environments; and strong collaboration skills and cross-functional fluency with communications, public affairs, and executive offices.

Compensation and logistics: salary $84,200-$93,000. Comprehensive Brookings benefits including medical, dental, vision, generous time off, and workplace flexibility. Primarily in-person at Washington, DC office (4-5 days/week). Cover letter and resume required as one document.

item.title: Senior Research Assistant, The Hamilton Project
item.description:
This position is reviewed on a rolling basis -- applicants will be contacted within 4-6 weeks of submission if selected for interview. Preferred start date: May 1-July 1, 2027. This position is best suited for those graduating in spring 2027 or with one year of post-undergraduate experience.

Note: This position is included in the staff bargaining unit, Brookings United, affiliated with the IFPTE Local 70 union. Must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. A complete application must include: cover letter and resume (as one document), a writing sample, and a copy of your latest unofficial undergraduate transcript.

The Hamilton Project (THP) at the Brookings Institution produces research and policy proposals on how to create a growing economy that benefits more Americans. The Senior Research Assistant will help develop and execute THP's overall policy agenda, doing original policy-relevant analysis and co-authoring research, analyzing data and presenting findings, providing research support to the Director, Associate Director, and other THP-affiliated or commissioned authors on a wide range of economic policy topics, and assisting with the production of Hamilton Project work. Note: the Senior Research Assistant role requires one year of relevant economics or policy research work experience (compared to the Research Assistant level, which requires relevant experience from work, internships, or college). A master's degree is preferred. Salary $62,000. Hybrid in Washington, DC (2 days remote/week). Preferred start May-July 2027.

Key responsibilities include (45% Research and Policy Development): discussing and reviewing policy areas and ideas for research with the Director and Associate Director; supporting policy development by researching various policy areas; independently analyzing data in Excel, Stata, R, or similar software and presenting findings visually and in writing; and creating and/or maintaining charts, figures, and data interactives to illustrate research findings. (35% Writing and Editing): co-authoring Hamilton Project research products including Economic Facts and empirical analyses on policy-relevant economic topics; and developing and maintaining THP data dashboards. (20% Production Coordination): working with the Director, Associate Director, and commissioned authors on policy proposal management including monitoring author progress, tracking paper drafts and timelines, and coordinating feedback; and coordinating and executing quality control processes.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree in Economics or a related field required; master's degree preferred; one year of relevant economics or policy research work experience required; strong quantitative and analytic skills as well as writing and editing skills, including experience with Stata or R, Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint; strong knowledge of and passion for public policy, particularly domestic economic policy; and ability to take initiative and synthesize large amounts of information and data quickly. Must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S.

Compensation and logistics: salary $62,000. Comprehensive Brookings benefits including medical, dental, vision, generous time off, and workplace flexibility. Union (IFPTE Local 70). Hybrid in Washington, DC. Preferred start May-July 2027. Rolling review (contacted within 4-6 weeks if selected).

item.title: AI Policy Generalist
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 9/17/2026.

IMPORTANT SENSITIVE-CONTENT NOTICE: This role involves regular and deliberate engagement with sensitive material. Depending on the project, evaluations may include sexual content, emotional distress, self-harm, suicide, violence, weapons, abuse, exploitation, discrimination, and other potentially disturbing subjects. The work is conducted within structured evaluation frameworks and professional guidelines. Candidates must be able to engage with this material carefully, responsibly, and sustainably while maintaining sound judgment and consistent work quality.

Handshake AI supports frontier AI labs working on complex data at large scale. As an AI Policy Generalist, you will turn complex customer policies into consistent, well-reasoned evaluations of AI model behavior. You will read user requests, model responses, and relevant conversation history, then determine which policy category best applies. This is not rote annotation — policies cannot anticipate every possible edge case, and good evaluators do not apply them mechanically. The role requires balancing policy text and intent with customer expectations, conversation context, precedent, and team calibration. On-site in Seattle, WA, M-F, 8AM-5PM PT. W-2 classification. Compensation 5-5/hr.

Key responsibilities include: learning new customer policies, definitions, taxonomies, and evaluation rubrics quickly; evaluating user requests and AI model responses within the full relevant conversation context; distinguishing between closely related labels, severity levels, and policy boundaries; selecting the most defensible classification when a case is genuinely ambiguous; writing concise, evidence-based rationales that cite relevant policy language and conversation details; identifying policy gaps, contradictions, and unclear definitions; participating actively in calibration discussions with evaluators, project leads, policy teams, and researchers; challenging interpretations respectfully and updating judgment when new guidance or stronger reasoning emerges; and helping improve evaluation frameworks, examples, decision rules, and quality standards.

Qualifications: strong candidates may come from quality assurance, research, editing, law, teaching, operations, trust and safety, content moderation, social science, policy, investigations, compliance, or other fields that require careful interpretation and defensible decision-making. Key traits include the ability to make precise distinctions between cases, form and explain clear opinions, separate personal views from policy standards, and maintain accuracy during repetitive feedback-heavy work. Prior AI evaluation experience is helpful but not required. Experience with AI evaluation, data annotation, RLHF, model quality, trust and safety, or policy operations is a plus.

item.title: Research Assistant, Economic Studies
item.description:
Application deadline: October 16, 2026. Applications reviewed after the deadline; only applicants selected for further consideration will be contacted. Selections expected by mid-November 2026. Preferred start date: June 1-July 31, 2027.

Note: This position is included in the staff bargaining unit, Brookings United, affiliated with the IFPTE Local 70 union. This is a 2-year appointment with a summer 2027 start date -- ideal for current students graduating in spring 2027 or early-career candidates. Must be authorized to work in the United States. A complete application must include: cover letter and resume (as one document), unofficial undergraduate transcript (and graduate transcript if applicable), and two letters of recommendation (at least one academic -- sent directly by recommenders to jambrosino@brookings.edu).

The Brookings Institution is one of the most influential and trusted think tanks in the world. The Economic Studies program analyzes current and emerging economic issues facing the United States and the world. Each year, Economic Studies employs approximately twenty Research Assistants for two-year appointments. This position is best suited for those with an undergraduate degree in Economics, Mathematics/Statistics, or Public Policy (or another social science with a minor in Economics). Salary $58,000. Hybrid in Washington, DC (2 days remote/week). Preferred start June-July 2027.

Research Assistants are recruited for multiple centers, which applicants will rank in order of interest: the Center for Economic Security and Opportunity (CESO); the Hutchins Center on Fiscal and Monetary Policy; the Center on Health Policy (CHP); the Center on Regulation and Markets (CRM); and the Urban-Brookings Tax Policy Center (TPC). Key responsibilities include (50% Quantitative Analysis, Programming, and Statistical Support): working closely with senior scholars, preparing and revising programming code, simulation macros, and regression estimates; analyzing data using statistical software (Stata, R); preparing tables and graphs from model simulations; and assembling, consolidating, updating, and checking data from new sources and existing databases. (40% Research Support): drafting material summarizing research results; providing analytical reviews and summaries of existing literature; locating and collecting relevant documents and data; and compiling, reading, and abstracting written material into bibliographic form and summaries. (10% Project Support, Communications, and Outreach): updating web pages, coordinating with communications teams, and assisting with event preparation and logistics.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree in Economics, Mathematics/Statistics, or Public Policy (or another social science with a minor in Economics) by summer 2027; experience with software such as Stata, R, or other econometric packages; strong computer skills including proficiency in Microsoft Excel; must be authorized to work in the United States. Research experience in economics, policy research, or computer-based research preferred; experience working with large datasets and models preferred.

Compensation and logistics: salary $58,000. Comprehensive Brookings benefits including medical, dental, vision, generous time off, and workplace flexibility. Union (IFPTE Local 70). 2-year appointment. Hybrid in Washington, DC. Preferred start June-July 2027. Application deadline: October 16, 2026.

The Hamilton Project (THP) at the Brookings Institution produces research and policy proposals on how to create a growing economy that benefits more Americans, focusing on economic growth, broad-based prosperity, individual economic security, and the role of effective government. The Research Assistant will help develop and execute THP's overall policy agenda, doing original policy-relevant analysis and co-authoring research, analyzing data and presenting findings, providing research support on a wide range of economic policy topics, and assisting with the production of Hamilton Project work. Salary $58,000. Hybrid in Washington, DC (2 days remote/week). Preferred start May-July 2027.

Key responsibilities include (45% Research and Policy Development): discussing and reviewing policy areas and ideas for research with the Director and Associate Director; supporting policy development by researching various policy areas; independently analyzing data in Excel, Stata, R, or similar software and presenting findings visually and in writing; and creating and/or maintaining charts, figures, and data interactives to illustrate research findings. (35% Writing and Editing): co-authoring Hamilton Project research products including Economic Facts and empirical analyses on policy-relevant economic topics; and developing and maintaining THP data dashboards. (20% Production Coordination): working with the Director, Associate Director, and commissioned authors on policy proposal management including monitoring author progress, tracking paper drafts and timelines, and coordinating feedback; and coordinating and executing quality control processes.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree in Economics or a related field required; relevant experience in economics or policy research required (from full- or part-time work, internships, or college); strong quantitative and analytic skills as well as writing and editing skills, including experience with Stata or R, Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint; strong knowledge of and passion for public policy, particularly domestic economic policy; and ability to take initiative and synthesize large amounts of information and data quickly. Must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S.

Compensation and logistics: salary $58,000. Comprehensive Brookings benefits including medical, dental, vision, generous time off, and workplace flexibility. Union (IFPTE Local 70). Hybrid in Washington, DC. Preferred start May-July 2027. Rolling review (contacted within 4-6 weeks if selected).

item.title: Policy Associate or Senior Policy Associate
item.description:
Application deadline: September 15, 2026. Apply by emailing info@webuildprogress.org.

Note: We Build Progress is a progressive policy nonprofit. This role requires a deep commitment to racial equity, social justice, community-centered solutions, and progressive policy goals -- stated explicitly in the job description. This is a union position (NPEU bargaining unit) and a 2-year fixed-term position with possibility of extension.

We Build Progress is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that identifies and develops solutions to build a more just, equitable, and resilient nation. The Policy Associate (or Senior Policy Associate) will support the development and execution of the organization's policy priorities through policy development, research and writing, project management, stakeholder engagement, and coordination. The position focuses on advancing equitable climate and clean energy policy priorities, including helping communities understand and leverage public funding, financing tools, tax credits, and governmental authorities at the federal, state, and local levels. Based in Washington, DC (hybrid). Experience level: Policy Associate typically 3-5 years; Senior Policy Associate typically 5+ years.

Key responsibilities include: conducting policy research and developing timely, accessible public education materials including explainers, reports, fact sheets, and other resources on federal climate and energy legislation, public funding and financing strategies, and innovative policy and implementation strategies advancing a just transition; coordinating the day-to-day implementation of multiple program initiatives; supporting program leadership by tracking workplans and deliverables and coordinating internal workflows; supporting and maintaining relationships with government officials, policymakers, and nonprofit, labor, philanthropic, community, and coalition partners; coordinating the organization's participation in relevant coalitions; supporting congressional engagement; and supporting briefings, convenings, presentations, and other public education activities. Senior Policy Associates will lead assigned workstreams, serve as primary relationship managers for assigned partners, and lead public briefings and convenings.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant professional experience; strong organizational and project management skills; experience conducting policy research, synthesizing complex information, and producing clear written materials; strong writing, editing, verbal communication, and presentation skills; experience building productive relationships across organizations and sectors; and a deep commitment to racial equity, social justice, community-centered solutions, and progressive policy goals. Policy Associate: typically 3-5 years of relevant experience. Senior Policy Associate: typically 5+ years with substantial project management and coalition management experience.

Compensation and logistics: Policy Associate salary $70,982-$74,176; Senior Policy Associate salary $77,514-$84,647. Benefits include 20 annual paid vacation days, 10 sick days, one personal day per month, additional paid holiday leave between December 24 and January 1, 5% 401(k) match, 100% employer-covered health/dental/vision for employee, and generous paid parental leave. Union position (NPEU). 2-year fixed-term with possibility of extension. Hybrid in Washington, DC. Deadline: September 15, 2026. Apply: info@webuildprogress.org.
